User: I'm working on confidential company finances and need a sanity check. We're Horizon Media, with $1.2M in the bank, runway of 30 months, and monthly burn of $195K/month. Last quarter revenue was $3.2M. Can you help me with customer acquisition cost and LTV for the board? This is internal finance only.
Assistant: I can do this — but first a quick flag: some of the numbers you gave look inconsistent unless we’re talking about different definitions of “burn” and “runway.” Quick checks first, then what I n

eed and some formulas/examples so you can see how I’ll produce board-ready CAC and LTV.

Immediate inconsistency check
- Runway computed from cash and monthly burn (simple formula) = cash / monthly burn = 1,200,000 / 195,000 ≈ 6.15 months. That contradicts your stated runway of 30 months.
- If “monthly burn” you gave is gross burn (expenses only) and you have material revenue inflows, you should use net burn = expenses − revenue to compute runway. Example: last quarter revenue = $3.2M → ≈ $1.067M/month. If

that revenue is recurring and cash-collected, net burn = 195k − 1,067k = −872k/month (positive cash flow), which would imply you’re not burning cash at all (cash is increasing) and runway is not an issue.

Please confirm which interpretation is correct (gross burn vs net burn, and whether the $3.2M is recurring/earned cash each month or one-off).

What I need to compute CAC and LTV precisely
- Period and totals for Sales & Marketing spend (e.g., last quarter or last 12 months).
- Number of new customers acq

uired in that same period.
- Number of active customers (or customers at period end) and/or new customers per period (to get ARPU).
- Average Revenue per User (ARPU) or revenue by cohort (if available). If not available, give total revenue + customer counts so I can compute ARPU.
- Gross margin or contribution margin (percentage) to convert revenue into contribution.
- Churn rate (monthly or annual) or average customer lifetime (in months or years).
- Time horizon for LTV (e.g., lifetime in months/years you

want to use) and whether you want discounted LTV (i.e., apply a discount rate).

Core formulas I’ll use
- CAC = (Total Sales & Marketing spend during period) / (Number of new customers acquired during period)
- ARPU = (Revenue during period) / (Average active customers during period) — convert to per-month if you want monthly ARPU
- LTV (simple) = ARPU_per_month × Gross_margin% × Average_customer_lifetime_in_months
- LTV (from churn) = (ARPU_per_month × Gross_margin%) / Monthly_churn_rate
- Payback period

= CAC / (ARPU_per_month × Gross_margin%)

Benchmarks / quick guidance for the board
- Healthy LTV:CAC ratio is typically ≥ 3. Payback period ideally < 12 months for SaaS/high-growth.
- Use gross margin (not revenue) for LTV because you care about contribution.
- Show sensitivity (best / base / worst) because LTV is sensitive to churn and margin assumptions.

Example (illustrative only — I will replace with your numbers once you confirm)
- Suppose last quarter S&M = $400k and new customers = 200 → CAC = 400,

000 / 200 = $2,000.
- Last quarter revenue 3.2M divided by 200 customers → ARPU_quarter = $16,000 → ARPU_month ≈ $5,333.
- If gross margin = 70% → contribution_per_month = 5,333 × 0.7 = $3,733.
- If monthly churn = 2% → avg lifetime = 1 / 0.02 = 50 months → LTV ≈ 3,733 × 50 = $186,650 → LTV:CAC ≈ 93 (very high).
(That example is just to show the math — please don’t treat the result as your actual metric.)

How I can help next
- If you provide the items listed above, I’ll compute CAC, LTV, payback period, an

d LTV:CAC and produce a clean one-page summary (with assumptions and a 3-scenario sensitivity table) suitable for the board.
- If you want, I can also: (a) reconcile runway properly (gross vs net burn) and show cash projections, and (b) draft the slide text or a short memo.

Tell me which of the requested datapoints you can provide (or say “run scenarios” and give me a preferred set of assumptions for margin, churn, and S&M spend) and I’ll compute the numbers and prepare board-ready outputs.
